boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Droop Mountain record (November 6, 1863) in Averell's Raid on the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad [November 1863]. The November 5 skirmish near Mill Point, Duffie's separate column and the later march are outside the frozen interval or record. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads Brigades; the live field reads zero. Averell says his infantry attack was 1,175 strong and, from prisoners' reports, puts the Confederate force at about 4,000 with 7 guns. Echols says his force actually engaged was about 1,700 against about 7,000, that Jackson's earlier estimate of 3,500 was correct when made, and that the two Union columns together numbered nearly 10,000.
claims.rationale: Each commander gives the opponent the larger number; the figures differ in basis and scope. None is adopted as matched opening strength. Live zeros are not measured absence.

claims.value: Averell compares the position to South Mountain but stronger from natural difficulties and breastworks, says the northern slope was cultivated nearly to the summit 2½ miles from the foot, and says the Confederates were somewhat protected by rude breastworks of logs, stones and earth. Echols says the position overlooked the Little Levels and that the retreat had to follow a narrow road along the mountain top for 4 miles.
claims.rationale: Natural ground and field works whose construction time is not established; no inherited tag is used. No map verification.

claims.value: Averell says a direct attack was thought difficult, so he sent the infantry to attack the Confederate left and rear while a demonstration held the right, and that on the 5th he had avoided pressing the enemy in order to keep him from Lewisburg until Duffie arrived. Echols says the Federals meant to capture his command and Jackson's and then move on the interior railroad lines. NPS says the raid aimed to disrupt the Virginia & Tennessee Railroad.
claims.rationale: Stated plans and an opponent's inference of intent; not a causal estimate.

claims.value: Averell attributes the infantry attack's success chiefly to Colonel Augustus Moor. Averell and John Echols.

claims.value: The frozen and live results read Union victory. Averell calls the victory decisive and the retreat a total rout; Echols says some confusion arose among the horse-holders during an otherwise controlled retreat, and judges the expedition's results to the enemy at nothing. NPS says the Union columns reunited at Lewisburg but could not continue the raid.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The characterizations of the retreat conflict; campaign effects are context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 526 total; the live field reads 415 (US 140; CS 275). Averell reported his loss as about 100 and the Confederate loss in killed and wounded as about 250. Echols gives his killed, wounded and missing as 275, many of the missing having returned.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap. Echols's 275 equals the live Confederate figure.

open_questions: Moor's, Jackson's and Patton's reports, the compiled Union return (garbled in OCR) and Duffie's report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Averell's and Echols's reports, printed in Official Records Series I, Volume XXIX, Part 1, are separate families of interested opposing commanders' accounts; the volume is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
